newsitem.title: VATICAN: Roman Catholic priest murdered in Rwanda - Pope.
newsitem.headline: Roman Catholic priest murdered in Rwanda - Pope.

text.p: A Roman Catholic priest was murdered on Sunday while he was celebrating mass at his parish church in northern Rwanda, Pope John Paul said.
He named the dead priest as missionary Guy Pinard.

"I have just received news of the tragic death of Father Guy Pinard...who was barbarically assassinated this morning while celebrating mass at his parish church in Ruhengeri, in Rwanda," the Pope told pilgrims in St Peter's Square.
"Let us pray to the Holy Virgin for him, for those who are dear to him and for his people, that they may again find peace and respect for life".
Pinard's nationality was not immediately clear and the Pope gave no other details.

More than half a million minority ethnic Tutsis and Hutu moderates died in 1994's Hutu-led ethnic slaughter in Rwanda, after which Tutsis swept to power and the perpetrators fled to neighbouring countries.

A new United Nations report said on Friday that Hutu death squads were killing Tutsi survivors of genocide and witnesses, who had been forced to move out of isolated areas to places near army positions and towns in search of security.

The report by the U.N. human rights office said survivors were being hunted down in their homes, intimidated, threatened and sometimes poisoned in remote areas of in the tiny central African country bordering Zaire.
The U.N. report said at least 227 genocide survivors were killed in 1996, when attacks against them rose sharply, and urged Rwanda to take measures to protect them.
Hutu militia among the 600,000 refugees who returned from Zaire late in 1996 were behind some of the attacks, the report said.
The mass influx from eastern Zaire and the expulsion of half a million Hutu refugees in Tanzania by troops in December have increased ethnic tensions in Rwanda.
